newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares revive despite political clouds.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares revive despite political clouds.

text.p: Hopes of an end to Turkey's protracted political crisis dragged shares out of the doldrums on Tuesday, but underlying concerns about the outcome of the coalition wrangling still hung over the market, brokers said.
The IMKB National-100 index ended the day up 3.61 percent, or 53 points, at 1,523. Trade volume jumped to 19.90 trillion lira ($142.5 million) from 13.43 trillion ($96.4 million) on Monday.

"The index's 1,440 support looked strong, so with the help of rising volume the market aimed to test the 1,530 resistance," said Goknur Karabiyik from Gedik Securities, saying the market would target a move to 1,590 if the cash influx continued.
The market was revived by speculation about a possible end to the Islamist-led government, brokers said.
Domestic speculators were behind the upward move, which was limited largely to blue chip stocks, such as utitilities and financials, according to Volkan Sari, market strategist at Global Securities.
The insurance sector led the uptrend, with leading companies rising seven percent.
But Sari said Tuesday's gains could not be sustained while the coalition stumbled on in a dispute with the secularist military and was unable to address urgent economic problems.
"The market is just looking for a new government in the short term, but in the long term it wants one which will attract major investment," Sari said.

The troubled coalition was holding its first cabinet meeting in eight weeks on Tuesday amid a deepening rift between Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's Islamists and conservatives. Speculation about its outcome restrained the market.
"As we ultimately remain tied to politics, the cabinet meeting will clarify the direction we will take," said Haldun Sertel, a broker at Can Securities.
The coalition partners went into the meeting deadlocked over an army-backed plan to restrict religious education as part of a campaign to erode support for Erbakan's Welfare Party.

A conservative minister said ahead of the cabinet talks that his True Path Party, led by pro-Western Tansu Ciller, was discussing the possibility of elections with Welfare. Four MPs from True Path have resigned in recent days, reducing the government's parliamentary majority on paper to one.
Financial markets have drifted downwards in tandem with the dwindling fortunes of the 11-month-old coalition, whose earlier bold promises for the economy had for a time won over market participants.
Optimism about the government's revenue-raising plans lifted shares over 60 percent in the first quarter of the year, but sustained government instability has destroyed market hopes.
Brokers said a sustained renewal of share gains was unlikely as long as efforts to tackle deep economic problems continued to take a back seat.
"I expect profit-taking after seeing these levels," said Mehmet Yildiz of Emper Securities.
Turkish bond yields climbed to 103-103.5 percent from 102.5 percent on Monday in subdued trade amid ongoing concerns over the government's fate.
The lira slipped to 139,640 to the dollar from a close on Monday of 139,300 close in line with dollar strength against the mark.
